metadata.case_name: WONG PUI SEUNG SHIRLEY v. COMMISSIONER OF THE INDEPENDENT COMMISSION AGAINST CORRUPTION

injuries.description: tenosynovitis, also known as de Quervain’s syndrome of both forearms and hands.
source: tenosynovitis, also known as de Quervain’s syndrome of both forearms and hands.
Dr Chu diagnosed tenosynovitis of both forearms and hands, specifically bilateral de Quervain’s tenosynovitis.
Dr Ip also diagnosed her as suffering from bilateral de Quervain’s disease
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injury of extensor muscle, fascia or tendon of thumb at wrist or hand level

injuries.description: mild tendonitis of the wrist extensors and flexors
source: Dr Ip also diagnosed her as suffering from bilateral de Quervain’s disease and mild tendonitis of the wrist extensors and flexors.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of other specified muscle, fascia or tendon at wrist or hand level

manifestations.description: constant dull aching pain and discomfort in the wrists, more severe over the radial aspect
tenderness over the extensor and abductor tendons of both thumbs
restriction of grip and pain over the tendons when the thumb movement was restricted and at the extremes of deviation
inability to type at high speed
unable to type for more than one hour per day (restriction on typing capacity)
difficulty in turning doorknobs and wringing out towels; could handle chopsticks no more than 10 minutes
occasional insomnia, stress; treated for Adjustment Disorder (psychiatric)
bilateral ganglia just distal to the radial styloid regions (clinical finding)

treatments_received: psychiatric treatment for Adjustment Disorder (treated until 29 March 2004)
voice-recognition (VR) typing system provided as an aid
treatments_future: release operation and excision of ganglia bilaterally with subsequent rehabilitation (recommended by Dr Ip)

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: Difficulty in carrying objects with hook grips; difficulty turning doorknobs and wringing towels; could handle chopsticks no more than 10 minutes

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Unable to enjoy sports which require strong thumb gripping

Permanent restriction in typing ability including inability to type at high speed and restriction to one hour of full-speed typing per day; adverse effect on employability as a translator and competition in the labour market
occasional insomnia, stress; treated for Adjustment Disorder (psychiatric)
